title: Property B: Independent Recoloring Cannot Beat Erdős — the Product-Space Repair Leaves the First-Moment Threshold Invariant
description: The open question property-b-first-moment-oq-03 asks to sharpen Erdős's 1963 bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) to the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) via the asymmetric/recoloring refinement of the first-moment argument. The RS program has two ingredients: asymmetry of the random coloring and a recoloring repair. The sibling oq-03-oq-01 settled asymmetry negatively. This entry isolates the recoloring ingredient and settles its naive (independent, product-space) version negatively too: if each vertex is independently recolored by flipping its color with probability p, the per-vertex final color stays uniform (vertexFinalProb p = 1/2 for all p), so a k-edge is monochromatic with probability exactly 2·(1/2)^k = 2^(1-k) regardless of p. Hence independent recoloring leaves the first-moment monochromatic probability — and the m < 2^(k-1) threshold — exactly invariant. The RS gain must come from recoloring only the vertices of dangerous edges in a fixed order (a conditional, non-product model), which this result formally isolates as the irreducible core. 6 theorems, 3 defs, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: Property B (Erdős 1963) asks for the minimum number m(k) of edges in a k-uniform hypergraph that is not 2-colorable. The first-moment method gives m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1): if fewer than 2^(k-1) edges, the expected number of monochromatic edges under a uniform random 2-coloring is below 1, so a proper coloring exists. Radhakrishnan and Srinivasan (2000) improved this to m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) using a two-stage argument: color uniformly, then recolor the vertices of the surviving monochromatic ('dangerous') edges, in a random order, each with a small probability p ≈ (log k)/k. The crucial subtlety is that the recoloring is conditional (only dangerous-edge vertices) and order-dependent — it is not an independent product-space operation. This entry makes that subtlety precise by proving the naive product-space recoloring is inert.
overview.problemStatement: Model the naive 'independent recoloring': after a uniform first round, flip each vertex's color independently with probability p. Show this leaves the first-moment analysis exactly where Erdős left it — the per-vertex final color stays uniform, every k-edge stays monochromatic with probability 2^(1-k), and the m < 2^(k-1) threshold is unmoved — so any genuine Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan improvement must use the conditional, order-dependent recoloring.
overview.text: A structural ORIENT result for the open question property-b-first-moment-oq-03, complementing the sibling 'asymmetry is worthless' (oq-03-oq-01) with 'independent recoloring is worthless'.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything follows from one collapse: the final color of a vertex is its uniform first-round color XOR an independent Bernoulli(p) flip, and P[final = target] = (1/2)(1−p) + (1/2)p = 1/2 by ring — the (1−p)+p cancellation. So vertexFinalProb p = 1/2 independent of p (vertexFinalProb_eq_half). By independence across the k vertices, monoIndep k p = 2·(vertexFinalProb p)^k = 2·(1/2)^k, which is monoOneStage k (monoIndep_eq_oneStage). Constancy in p (monoIndep_const, expMono_indep_const) is then immediate. The threshold equivalence m·monoIndep k p < 1 ↔ 2m < 2^k is closed-form real arithmetic: rewrite 2·(1/2)^k = 2/2^k and apply div_lt_one with 2^k > 0 (threshold_indep). The closed form monoOneStage k = 2^(1-k) is exhibited via zpow lemmas (monoOneStage_eq_zpow).
keyInsights: XOR-ing a uniform bit with an independent flip is uniform: the per-vertex final color probability is 1/2 for every flip rate p, so independent recoloring carries no information.
Therefore the monochromatic probability of a k-edge is exactly the Erdős value 2^(1-k) under the independent two-stage model — the repair is provably inert.
The first-moment threshold m < 2^(k-1) is invariant under independent recoloring: no choice of p moves it, mirroring the sibling result that no bias moves it.

Consequently the entire Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan gain of order √(k/log k) is attributable to the conditional, order-dependent structure of the true recoloring (only dangerous-edge vertices, in a fixed order) — a non-product model that this product-space argument cannot, and is shown not to, capture.
Modeling probabilities as real-valued functions (not a measure space) suffices to settle the negative direction rigorously and cheaply, exactly as in the sibling entries.

sections.title: Overview: Independent Recoloring Is Inert
sections.summary: Module docstring framing this as the recoloring companion to the sibling 'asymmetry is worthless' result (oq-03-oq-01): under the naive independent (product-space) recoloring model, the first-moment monochromatic probability and Erdős's threshold m < 2^(k-1) are exactly unchanged for every flip rate p.
sections.mathContext: The docstring states the whole result chain: vertexFinalProb p = 1/2, monoIndep k p = monoOneStage k = 2^(1-k), and the invariant threshold m < 2^(k-1).

sections.title: The Independent Two-Stage Recoloring Model
sections.summary: Three definitions modeling the naive recoloring: vertexFinalProb p (per-vertex final-color probability after an independent flip), monoIndep k p (k-edge monochromatic probability under that model), and monoOneStage k (the one-round Erdős baseline 2·(1/2)^k).

sections.title: The Per-Vertex Final Color Stays Uniform
sections.summary: vertexFinalProb p = (1/2)(1−p) + (1/2)p = 1/2 for all p (vertexFinalProb_eq_half): XOR of a uniform first-round color with an independent flip is uniform.
sections.mathContext: The single algebraic collapse from which the whole inertness of independent recoloring follows.

sections.title: Monochromatic Probability Is the Erdős Value, for Every p
sections.summary: monoIndep_eq_oneStage: monoIndep k p = monoOneStage k = 2·(1/2)^k; monoOneStage_eq_zpow exhibits 2^(1-k); monoIndep_const and expMono_indep_const record constancy in p.
sections.mathContext: The independent two-stage model reproduces the one-round monochromatic probability identically.

sections.title: The First-Moment Threshold Is Unmoved
sections.summary: threshold_indep: m·monoIndep k p < 1 ↔ 2m < 2^k — exactly Erdős's m < 2^(k-1), independent of the flip rate p.
sections.mathContext: Quantifies inertness: independent recoloring cannot raise the threshold, isolating the conditional recoloring as the sole remaining lever.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 111 lines, 6 theorems and 3 definitions proving that independent (product-space) recoloring leaves the Property B first-moment analysis exactly invariant: the per-vertex final color stays uniform, every k-edge stays monochromatic with probability 2^(1-k), and the m < 2^(k-1) threshold does not move, for any flip rate p.
conclusion.implications: Together with the sibling 'asymmetry is worthless' result, this eliminates both naive shortcuts to the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan bound and converts the knowledge-base observation 'the recoloring step is not expressible by summing over a single product sample space V → Bool' into a theorem. The remaining work — the conditional, order-dependent recoloring of dangerous-edge vertices with p ≈ (log k)/k — is thereby sharply isolated as the irreducible core of the open question.
openQuestions: Formalize the conditional recoloring: recolor only vertices lying in first-round monochromatic edges, in a fixed (random) order, and bound the probability that any edge is monochromatic afterwards — the genuine two-stage RS model that this entry shows the product model cannot capture.
Establish the single-edge conditional recoloring expectation and the union bound over m edges (roadmap steps 1–2), then the p = (log k)/k optimization yielding the √(k/log k) factor (step 3).
Connect the conditional recoloring to a measure-theoretic probability space in Mathlib (PMF / product measures with conditioning) to move beyond the real-valued-function first-moment idiom.

mainTheorems.name: vertexFinalProb_eq_half
mainTheorems.description: After an independent flip-with-probability-p recoloring of a uniformly colored vertex, the final color stays uniform: (1/2)(1−p) + (1/2)p = 1/2, for every p.

mainTheorems.name: monoIndep_eq_oneStage
mainTheorems.description: Independent recoloring is worthless: a k-edge is monochromatic with the one-round Erdős probability 2·(1/2)^k = 2^(1-k) for every flip rate p.
mainTheorems.leanType: (k : ℕ) → (p : ℝ) → monoIndep k p = monoOneStage k

mainTheorems.name: threshold_indep
mainTheorems.description: The first-moment threshold is unmoved by independent recoloring: m·monoIndep k p < 1 ↔ 2m < 2^k, i.e. exactly Erdős's m < 2^(k-1).
mainTheorems.leanType: (m k : ℕ) → (p : ℝ) → (m * monoIndep k p < 1 ↔ 2 * m < 2 ^ k)

mainTheorems.name: monoOneStage_eq_zpow
mainTheorems.description: The one-round monochromatic probability in closed form as a real integer power: 2^(1-k).

mainTheorems.name: expMono_indep_const
mainTheorems.description: The expected number of monochromatic edges m·monoIndep k p is independent of the flip rate p.
mainTheorems.leanType: (m k : ℕ) → (p q : ℝ) → (m * monoIndep k p = m * monoIndep k q)
